Title: Build more responsive apps with the Decisions API

URL Source: https://openai.com/index/decisions-api

Markdown Content:
Applications and agents make many small decisions throughout a workflow: how to classify an input, where to route a request, or which action to take next. Individually, they are simple. At scale, their latency and cost add up.

Today, we’re making the Decisions API generally available. Built with [GPT‑6 Luna](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-sol-and-luna/), the Decisions API focuses Luna’s intelligence on questions with bounded answers, helping applications and agents make near real-time decisions from text, images, and structured inputs up to 10x faster than GPT‑6 Luna through the Responses API.

Since public beta, we’ve added a native GPT‑Live integration, prompt caching for reused context, and inference residency in the US and EU. Developers can also pass native JSON inputs, include images in question instructions, and ask up to 400 questions per request, twice the previous limit. We’ve also continued to improve latency, including additional capacity in several regions in Asia.

## How teams are using the Decisions API

Early adoption of Decisions has shown its applicability across a variety of use cases.

Across OpenAI, teams are applying the Decisions API across product and business workflows. The dots team is using it to reduce response times and improve interactivity. Our Personal Finance team is using it to categorize transaction descriptions, while our Communications team is using Decisions to classify coverage by the themes and scores whether it reinforces or challenges key narratives—helping identify what warrants closer review.

These early examples show how fast, structured decision-making can turn incoming information into useful action across a wide range of use cases. Customers are applying the Decisions API just as broadly, from accurately attributing AI costs to making language-learning experiences more interactive.

1 of 5

## Select the type of decision your application needs

Using the Decisions API is simple: developers define a question and its allowed answers, then provide context as text, images, or native JSON. The API returns one of three supported answer types—a probability, choice, or score—that applications can use to determine what happens next. The variety of answer types allows Decisions to be applicable across a wide variety of use cases.

Decisions API supports three answer types:

| Type | Use it to | Main result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| predicate | Estimate the probability that a condition is true, such as whether a product has visible damage. | probability: an estimate from 0 to 1 that the condition is true. |
| choice | Select one of your predefined options, such as whether an agent should continue, retry, or ask for clarification. | choice: one of your supplied values. The response also includes probabilities and confidence. |
| score | Rate an input against ordered levels in a rubric, such as the severity of damage. | score: the probability-weighted average of the level indices. |

## Build real-time voice experiences with the Decisions API and GPT‑Live

With [GPT‑Live](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-live-1-in-the-api/), you can bring natural, expressive conversation to your voice applications, with smooth interruption handling that keeps conversations flowing. Decisions API now [integrates natively with GPT‑Live⁠(opens in a new window)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions-voice), helping applications make fast, focused decisions during live conversations. A customer support agent can decide whether to ask a clarifying question, route a request, or escalate an issue. An avatar can adjust its facial expressions as a user speaks to it, and based on the user’s words, respond with a wink or a smile to create a more interactive experience.

The example below uses transcript updates to select an avatar’s expression. Add this configuration to `session.triggers` in an existing GPT‑Live session.

Live emits a `decision.event`; the application reads the selected `reaction` and animates the character accordingly. [Learn more about connecting voice to Decisions API. ⁠(opens in a new window)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions-voice)

## Try Decisions with GPT‑Live for yourself

## Expression palette

Tap a face to preview it.

## Live decisions

Watch as the Decisions API chooses a facial expression based on what each of you says.

### Your words

Watch the reaction as you speak.

### Assistant’s words

Watch the face as the assistant replies.

Try saying

I rehearsed my audition for my cat. She walked out halfway through.

This demo is time-limited. By using it, you agree to OpenAI's [Terms⁠](https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use/) and acknowledge our [Privacy Policy⁠](https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy/).

## Build and evaluate your first decision

Decisions API is generally available today with GPT‑6 Luna through the dedicated Decisions endpoint. See the [pricing and availability guide⁠(opens in a new window)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions#pricing-and-availability) for current rates and caching details.

Start with one recurring decision your application makes often. Define the question, the possible answers, and the context needed to distinguish them. Test it on examples that reflect real usage, in the [Decisions Playground⁠(opens in a new window)](https://platform.openai.com/decisions) with your own text or images, or follow the [developer guide⁠(opens in a new window)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions) to make your first request.

Decisions API costs $0.10 per million input tokens. Cached input costs $0.01 per million tokens. For 30-minute and 12-hour cached writes, [read our pricing guide.⁠(opens in a new window)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing?utm_source=chatgpt.com) You only pay for input tokens: there are no output-token charges. Regional processing is available in the US and EU, and [Zero Data Retention⁠(opens in a new window)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data) is available to eligible customers. See [pricing and caching⁠(opens in a new window)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions#pricing-and-availability) and [data controls ⁠(opens in a new window)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data)for details.

Title: What FDE means at OpenAI

URL Source: https://openai.com/index/forward-deployed-engineering-means

Markdown Content:
When Codex came out, someone on the team asked me, “What do we do when Codex can just one-shot the use cases we spent the last few months building?”

That question gets to the heart of what FDE means at OpenAI. We work alongside customers to understand their hardest problems and build solutions they can depend on. What we learn helps shape our products and gives Research concrete problems to solve.

That is progress. If we make ourselves obsolete every couple of months, our FDE team is doing its job.

I founded the team in early 2025 to close what we call**“the deployment gap”:**the distance between what models appear capable of and what people can reliably use to do their work.

Model capabilities have moved faster than the systems and processes needed to put them to use. Sometimes the missing piece is a product. Sometimes a model performs well on a benchmark but cannot do the job with real-life variables and constraints.

We focus on customers’ hardest problems. Where our models can do the job today, we work with Product and our customer to make the solution repeatable and, where they fall short, we work with customers and Research to define the gap and make improvements. Our goal is for each engagement to leave the next customer with a better starting point—if we raise the floor to the point our customers don’t need FDEs to solve this class of problem the next time, we have done our job well.

The challenge for [John Deere](https://openai.com/index/john-deere-justin-rose/), a 200 year-old agriculture business, was how to scale personalized advice for farmers.

One example is See & Spray, its precision weed-control technology, which uses cameras and machine learning to identify and spray weeds rather than treating entire fields to reduce chemical use by up to 70%.

But realizing those benefits depends on farmers knowing how to configure the technology, plan their season, and adjust their practices as conditions change.

John Deere deployed OpenAI’s APIs to help make that support personalized and scalable.

AI can answer farmers’ questions in natural language, provide tailored setup guidance and recommendations, identify when equipment may not be delivering its full potential, and help farmers understand the value they’re getting from the technology.

The opportunity extends beyond any single interaction: to deliver relevant guidance throughout the customer journey, helping farmers make better use of their equipment while improving efficiency and sustainability.

This is the kind of challenge OpenAI FDEs work to solve: helping organizations move from AI capabilities to systems that deliver practical value in complex, real-world environments.

But the problems are often wide open, there may be no established ground truth, and there is no playbook.**Everyone wants to build something that has never existed. Fewer people want to do what it takes to get there.**

Finding talented FDEs while raising the baseline for “good enough” has meant constant experimentation and application.

## Start with the outcome

At the start of every FDE team session, I put up a slide with one core value: “Start with the outcome, do what it takes to succeed, then follow with scale”.

An impressive demo can go a long way before anyone asks whether it works in the real world.

Our job is to solve the customer’s problem to a standard we can stand behind in production.

In mid-2025, we had around 15 FDEs working with a large semiconductor customer on 10+ use cases. The ambition was to make their verification process AI-native, covering:

*   Directed test generation

*   Root cause analysis and debugging

*   An architecture assistant

Verification can account for ~70% of a project’s effort in this industry. The opportunity was enormous, and there were many possible places to start.

Some FDEs had joined OpenAI just days earlier and had never worked in semiconductors. They embedded with the customer’s verification team, studied chip design in their spare time, and built evals with the engineers to test whether the AI could generate useful tests and correctly diagnose chip failures.

Alongside that learning, we built custom harnesses for the individual use cases. Over the first 3-6 months, all of them reached production and early user adoption. The payoff was seeing the metrics:

*   ~48% time saved through AI-based directed test generation.

*   22% median performance improvement through kernel optimisation.

*   Weeks of debugging compressed into hours

When we played this all back the Chief Hardware Officer asked, “Did you guys work as chip designers before coming here?”

**Our FDEs don’t****need to know the industry on day one but it is their responsibility to learn it.**

As coding assistants make software faster to build, understanding the customer’s business becomes even more important. We build teams with a mix of generalists and domain experts.

You need enough knowledge to make sound judgments, and **enough curiosity to question assumptions about the status quo.**

In life sciences, for example, our FDEs’ scientific backgrounds help them earn trust with researchers working on pre-clinical drug discovery tasks such as target validation and prioritization, gene-expression analysis, and chemical synthesis-route reconstruction. That expertise lets them contribute informed judgment about how those workflows could improve.

## M ake success repeatable

We had shown that these workflows could deliver value, but each still required too much custom integration to extend to another team. The next challenge was to preserve those results while making the software easier to deploy and maintain.

By then, Codex had grown in capability. One FDE tested rebuilding their application around it, then worked with the team to move the use cases onto a common harness with Codex at its core.

Custom applications became plugins and skills built on common Codex primitives. Codex also became the interface, allowing us to retire the separate terminal UIs and CLIs we had written for individual use cases.

We were able to remove roughly 90% of the custom code from each project, and this changed how we built, maintained and scaled these workflows:

*   We could benefit from centralized improvements to Codex, reducing the amount of glue code required for each individual use case

*   Key functionalities were bundled as skills and plugins, making them easier to share with each other and to be centrally controlled by the AI CoE. This meant that extending from one team to the next could be as simple as swapping in new connectors/MCP servers, building fresh evals (which we also had a skill for) and getting up and running.

*   In one August 2026 example, the initial deployment took two months. Extending the solution to a second team took one day. The next teams onboarded faster as we scaled—this has continued, with a use case in August 2026 taking 1 day for the second team after the initial deployment took 2 months.

That is one version of making ourselves obsolete. The work we had done to reach production established what mattered. As the underlying product improved, we could replace much of our custom implementation and keep the value it delivered.

_This is why the order matters. LLMs let us build fast. Use that speed to get something valuable into users’ hands, learn what holds up in practice, and then scale what works._

The same principle applies across all engagements.

[OpenAI Presence](https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/), our product for enterprise voice and chat agents, grew out of real customer deployments. The work began with [Swarm⁠(opens in a new window)](https://github.com/openai/swarm) and evolved through the [Agents API](https://openai.com/index/introducing-the-agents-api/), and today one customer now handles more than half of its calls with AI.

Getting those deployments into production taught us which problems needed a custom solution and which building blocks other teams could use. We brought those building blocks into Presence, making it easier for developers to automate regulated workflows without rebuilding the underlying infrastructure. Each deployment helped shape the product and gave the next customer a better starting point.

With [Thrive Holdings](https://openai.com/index/building-self-improving-tax-agents-with-codex/), OpenAI FDEs and researchers worked alongside engineers and accountants to build Tax AI for Crete’s accounting firms. During its pilot, Tax AI processed 7,000 tax returns and increased throughput by about 50%.

One of the hardest challenges was automating rental-property returns, which required six weeks of engineering and practitioner review to reach 90% precision and recall. The work created reusable patterns that made it easier to extend Tax AI to other complex tax schedules.

The teams are now applying the same approach to bookkeeping, audit, and IT support—building systems that improve through practitioner feedback and real-world use.

## Close the intelligence gaps as they appear

Sometimes a better product lets us simplify what we built but sometimes the model itself cannot yet do the job.

If we only build what today’s models already make possible, we will not uncover the intelligence gaps Research needs to close next. Therefore a lot of our important engagements start at those limits with the customer, FDE and Research committed to working through them together.

We had already developed a customer-service platform with a large telecommunications customer, and they wanted to extend it to voice.

Voice accounted for around 90% of their customer-service volume. These cases were more expensive to contain than chat, and brought a range of new technical challenges in getting accents, tone and latency/accuracy up to production grade. Getting it right would make a substantial difference to their business.

During scoping, our model scored around 60% on the key evals we used to assess whether it could do the job in production. We had reached the limits of its capabilities. Function calling and instruction following in customer-service scenarios needed to improve.

We explained that to the customer and brought Research into the work. FDE worked with the customer to build the platform and define what the model needed to do. Research worked on closing the capability gaps, with successive model snapshots letting us test progress against the customer’s requirements.

Over six months, performance on the key evals rose from around 60% to 80% and then 90%+, reaching the levels needed for production.

The resulting voice model now supports that customer’s deployment, other custom customer-service deployments, and managed deployments through Presence. A problem encountered in one customer’s business helped identify improvements that could serve many others.

Each part mattered. The customer committed to working on a problem the model could not yet solve. FDE stayed close enough to frame that problem, build the platform and drive the engagement from start to finish. Research improved the underlying model capabilities.

This is the other version of making ourselves obsolete: helping turn a problem today’s models cannot solve into a capability future models can deliver. The return on our work extends beyond the hours we spend with any one customer.

## Go find the harder problem

I joined OpenAI to help make AI useful in people’s everyday work. That still guides the team. I often say to the team that in most cases in LLM development, Occam’s Razor applies—the simplest solution is the best. In a company that is defined by its cutting edge research and in an industry that is tainted by hyperbole, we want to build stuff that works reliably which people in the field can depend on.

# NVIDIA Unveils Minerva to Bring End-to-End Observability for AI Factories

 New AIOps platform connects infrastructure and workload telemetry to help operators increase uptime and maximize AI factory yield.

October 22, 2026 by[Brian Sparks](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/author/bsparks/ "Posts by Brian Sparks")

 Share

Share This Article

Launched today, [NVIDIA Minerva](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/networking/products/software/minerva/) is an AIOps platform built to help teams find problems earlier and keep AI factories productive. It brings together telemetry from infrastructure and AI workloads, then applies purpose-built AI models to turn that data into timely, actionable insight.

AI factories are among the most complex operations in the world, with vast numbers of GPUs working across high-speed networks to train models and serve AI applications. At that scale, a single degraded component can slow an entire job. The warning signs may be easy to miss, such as a GPU running hotter than its peers or an NVMe drive losing performance under load.

The platform focuses on AI factory yield, a measure of the useful work infrastructure produces through GPU hours, goodput, cluster uptime and token production.

## **Delivering a Dynamic View of an AI Factory**

Traditional monitoring tools often divide the data center into separate views. Networking, compute, site reliability and machine learning teams each see a different part of the operation. Minerva connects those signals across NVIDIA GPUs, networking, storage, schedulers and workloads.

With these signals, Minerva builds a dynamic knowledge graph that logically maps the infrastructure — GPUs, SuperNICs, switches and cables — and the jobs running on it. This context helps operators trace a slow training job to the component affecting it, even across a factory with hundreds of thousands of GPUs.

It analyzes billions of data points per hour using supervised and unsupervised machine learning. It learns normal behavior, detects previously unseen anomalies, predicts emerging failures and correlates related events based on the factory’s topology. Instead of sending every symptom to an operator, it can group an event storm into a focused incident with a likely root cause.

Minerva comes with a native AI assistant and connects to external agentic AI tools. This adds a natural-language interface grounded in live telemetry. Operators can investigate cluster health and receive recommended remediation through conversation. Teams can keep a person in the loop to manually implement fixes or connect Minerva to automation through infrastructure application programming interfaces and external systems.

## **Results That Maximize AI Factory Yield**

The ability to correlate workload and infrastructure issues along with its agentic AI capabilities help simplify AI factory operations. Instead of dealing with a blizzard of alerts, Minerva aggregates related problems into a single actionable item. This allows AIOps teams to move from reactive to proactive maintenance. And all of this helps AI factories maximize GPU uptime.

Minerva delivers value for the key metrics AI factories focus on:

*   **Longer time between interruptions**: Minerva spots trouble before it happens, so jobs run longer without incident.
*   **Faster time to repair**: When an incident does happen, Minerva pinpoints the problem, leading to a significantly quicker resolution.
*   **Greater insight**: Modern AI infrastructure generates a flood of data; Minerva filters it out, leaving only the handful of alerts that actually matter.

IREN is among the NVIDIA partners using Minerva to optimize its AI factories.

“As we scale our AI factories, the key to providing the best service for our customers is maximizing the productivity of our GPUs,” said Denis Skrinnikoff, chief technology officer of IREN. “NVIDIA Minerva gives our operations team one view across the network, the GPUs and the jobs running on them, so we focus more on proactive maintenance rather than troubleshooting. That visibility strengthens our operating model for the infrastructure we’re building next.”

Joining IREN, Aolani, [Bitdeer AI](https://www.bitdeer.ai/en/blog/nvidia-minerva/), IBM, Jio,Lambda, Quake AI and Tesla plan to deploy Minerva.

In addition to Dell Technologies, [Lenovo](https://news.lenovo.com/europes-ai-moment-gtc-berlin-26)and [Supermicro](https://learn-more.supermicro.com/data-center-stories/supermicro-nvidia-minerva-supercloud-ai-factory)will offer Minerva as part of their AI factory operations portfolios.

Title: Cloud Deployment Incoming: ‘Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’ Arrives on GeForce NOW

URL Source: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/geforce-now-thursday-call-of-duty-modern-warfare-4/

Published Time: 2026-10-22T13:00:20+00:00

Markdown Content:
Lock in and load out this GFN Thursday. _Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4_ arrives on [GeForce NOW](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/?ncid=pa-srch-goog-673352&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=24109411186&gbraid=0AAAAAD4XAoFI7HGI1e1ouyUf4Z1vqL6Yj&gclid=Cj0KCQjw5vLVBhCiARIsAD56SFLLXG-prLkw0jX3AoX_rJn-CLfJKlNygVblhTr8HBpxVWSPe9WUkusaAvP1EALw_wcB) at launch, bringing a new campaign, multiplayer action and DMZ, high-stakes extraction mode to [supported devices](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/system-reqs/#windows-pc). The campaign also gets an enhanced look: GeForce RTX 5080-class performance arrives for Ultimate members, bringing support for ray-tracing features in the cloud.

There’s a new way to join the cloud, too: Existing supported Fire TV Stick users can now purchase one-month Performance or Ultimate memberships directly through Amazon, making it easier to sign up and start streaming on the big screen.

Plus, Square Enix’s _FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE_ brings cinematic pixel art and strategic battles to the cloud, and _The Elder Scrolls Online’s Echoes of Skyrim_ Season adds the entire Greymoor Chapter free for all ESO Standard Edition owners.

It’s all part of six games joining the [GeForce NOW library](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/games/) this week.

## **Deployment Without the Downloads**

_Squad up and answer the call on the cloud._

Activision and Infinity Ward’s _Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4_ launches today on GeForce NOW. Members can drop into the trenches in Korea, close-quarter combat in New York, high-octane chases through Paris, night raids in Mumbai and city-wide engagements to reclaim occupied territory.

Fight as Private Park, a young South Korean soldier facing live combat for the first time alongside his squad as a routine patrol turns into a desperate fight for survival. Beyond the front lines, operator-turned-outlaw Captain Price is operating outside the system he once served, pursuing revenge through covert missions as the conflict spreads.

Multiplayer pairs precise combat with fluid movement, a dozen core 6v6 maps from around the world and battlegrounds that are shaped by the campaign’s global conflict. The DMZ extraction mode sends players into contested territory to recover valuable technology, weigh objectives and decide when to get out. Loot, fight, negotiate, betray and extract — it’s all fair in the cloud and battleground.

[Ultimate members](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/premium-memberships/) can now experience the campaign with ray tracing, powered by newly added GeForce RTX 5080-class performance across PCs, Macs, handhelds, mobile devices, browsers, supported TVs and more. With game downloads and installs handled by GeForce NOW, members can spend less time preparing a local rig and more time preparing the next loadout.

## **A New Way to Play**

A new way to join GeForce NOW on Fire TV.

GeForce NOW in-app purchase is rolling out to existing supported Fire TV Stick users, making it possible to purchase a [membership](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/premium-memberships/) directly through Amazon using an existing account. Transactions are processed through Amazon’s billing system, creating a more seamless path from setup to gameplay.

GeForce NOW transforms Fire TV into a powerful PC gaming rig in the cloud. Members can stream supported PC games they already own or purchase new titles from digital stores including Steam, Epic Games Store, Ubisoft Connect, Xbox PC Game Pass, GOG and EA.

The library includes thousands of ready-to-play games, including many of the world’s most-played titles and more than 100 free-to-play games. No downloads, installs, patches or updates stand between a new game and playtime. An Amazon Fire TV Stick, the GeForce NOW app and an Ultimate membership are all it takes to level up the living room with GeForce RTX 5080-powered gaming.

## **A Pixel-Perfect Fantasy**

_Classic roots. A new adventure._

Square Enix’s _FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE_ launches today on GeForce NOW, bringing the series’ classic roots into a cinematic pixel-art world.

Travel with companions bound by fate and uncover the truth behind a force threatening to bring everything to ruin. Strengthen the party with Visions of beloved _FINAL FANTASY_ characters, each bringing unique skills and abilities to battle. Dynamic camera angles and pixelized 3D models give familiar fantasy a fresh perspective.

Exploit enemy weaknesses to stagger foes, break their defenses and seize extra turns before finishing the bonus phase with powerful Resonance attacks. Airships, crystals, espers and moogles bring familiar series favorites to a world filled with secrets to discover.

GeForce NOW handles the game’s downloads and storage in the cloud, leaving more space on supported devices for everyday essentials. Save the inventory management for potions and Phoenix Downs.

## **Step Into a New Season in Tamriel**

_Familiar lands. Fresh reasons to return._

_The Elder Scrolls Online_’s [second season](https://www.elderscrollsonline.com/en-us/news/post/70213), _Echoes of Skyrim_, launched Wednesday, Oct. 21, free for all ESO players and ready to stream through GeForce NOW.

Season Two gives everyone who owns ESO Standard Edition access to its Skyrim content and the Antiquities treasure-hunting system. The _Markarth_ downloadable content follows Monday, Nov. 9, rounding out the additions with two classic zones to explore.

The Season also introduces Solo Dungeons, reimagining challenges previously designed for groups. Moon Hunter Keep and March of Sacrifices have been redesigned and rebalanced for players ready to tackle their dangers alone. Earn new rewards and take on new challenges at your own pace without needing to find a group.

A new Tamriel Tome also launched Oct. 21, offering both free and premium battle pass reward tracks.

In addition, members can look for the following titles joining the [GeForce NOW library](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/games/) this week:

*   _We Were Here Tomorrow_ (New release on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2315050?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now), Oct. 20)
*   _FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE_ (New release on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3259780?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now), Oct. 22)
*   _Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4_(New release on Oct 23, available in the _Call of Duty_ app)
*   _CONTROL Resonant_([Epic Game Store](https://www.epicgames.com/store/p/control-resonant-3568d3?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now))
*   _Crimson Desert_([Epic Games Store](https://www.epicgames.com/store/p/crimson-desert-6d6135?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now))
*   _Planet Zoo 2_([Xbox app](https://www.xbox.com/games/store/planet-zoo-2/9nb4jf6b6vsf?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now), supports XBOX Play Anywhere)

Dates listed above reflect when games are released on their respective stores. GeForce NOW availability may vary, as games are onboarded after release and added throughout the week. Keep an eye on GeForce NOW channels and GFN Thursdays for availability updates on announced titles.

Gamers who want to test out high-performance GeForce NOW cloud gaming can start with a [day pass](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/?ncid=pa-srch-goog-673352&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=24109411186&gbraid=0AAAAAD4XAoGPVGKakiCteqkRtoF1Q-KSI&gclid=CjwKCAjws_DTBhB_EiwAXZknGUBjXpM5vNQvnwLXUGilFsIHBSkbKPfllg7RGpFFuQZv2GFityJC6BoCq8MQAvD_BwE) to try premium cloud gaming before committing to a membership. Better yet, the cost of the day pass can be applied toward a first monthly membership — making it easy to try GeForce RTX-powered cloud gaming with the latest releases, then level up for more.

What’s on the mission board this weekend? Let us know on [X](https://x.com/NVIDIAGFN) or in the comments below.

# Leading European Financial Services Organizations Embrace Open Models to Build Proprietary Intelligence

 From transaction foundation models to sovereign cloud deployments, leading financial institutions across Europe are scaling intelligent technologies with advanced computing.

October 21, 2026 by[Jason Renders](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/author/jasonrenders/ "Posts by Jason Renders")

 Share

Share This Article

At GTC Berlin, banks, payment companies and financial data providers are showing what production-scale intelligence looks like — built on NVIDIA accelerated computing, powered by open weight models and running on their own infrastructure.

Revolut is rebuilding its technology stack on a single foundation model [PRAGMA](https://resources.nvidia.com/en-us-financial-services-industry/revolut-builds-a-transaction-foundation-model-1185435), powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing. Using the [NVIDIA cuDF](https://developer.nvidia.com/topics/ai/data-science/cuda-x-data-science-libraries/cudf) toolkit and [Dynamo-Triton software](https://developer.nvidia.com/dynamo-triton) on [NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/technologies/blackwell-architecture/), Revolut is scaling PRAGMA in production, servicing an initial 80 million customers and engineered to scale 3x.

“Revolut processes billions of transactions — the opportunity was always there, but the question was whether foundation models could operate at that scale and across domains. PRAGMA answers that,” said Pavel Nesterov, head of AI at Revolut. “Built in collaboration with NVIDIA, it’s the clearest proof yet that the gap between a research breakthrough and a production banking system can be closed.”

## **Training on Accelerated Infrastructure**

Starling Bank, the first bank to train an agentic model on U.K. sovereign cloud infrastructure, has developed “Starling Intelligence” — the intelligence layer that underpins its AI capability — on Civo’s U.K. cloud using the bank’s own transaction data.

Lloyds Banking Group built [ATUM](https://medium.com/ai-at-lloyds-banking-group/introducing-atum-a-foundation-model-for-banking-4d5291577d50), a transaction foundation model that converts billions of banking transactions into reusable intelligence — accelerated with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs and improving efficiency across bank-wide use cases.

SBS launched a banking sovereign intelligence platform so banks can run generative and agentic models without their data leaving their own walls.

## **Open Models at a Fraction of the Cost**

Open weight models give European financial institutions proprietary intelligence built on data they own, at costs they control. NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform is the engine running beneath them.

Neobank bunq’s agentic assistant Finn now runs on open weight models. Powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, deploying on Nebius matches the quality of leading closed models at 60% of the cost per answer.

NatWest is building technology designed to recognize the full range of British accents, dialects and financial terminology, developed with NVIDIA’s speech models, including Nemotron 3.5 ASR.

Modulr is building specialized models for distinct parts of payment operations, based on the NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B open model.

Santander is an early adopter of the new NVIDIA Kumo family of open weight foundation models for structured financial data, using them to build specialized intelligence for core banking workloads.

## **Accelerated Computing Transforms Financial Research**

LSEG is working with NVIDIA to help financial institutions analyze large volumes of historical tick data up to 10x faster with the [Polars GPU engine](https://docs.pola.rs/user-guide/lazy/gpu/), accelerated by NVIDIA cuDF on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs.

RavenPack built a dataset generation pipeline on Bigdata.com that takes a plain-language research hypothesis and returns a labeled, backtest-ready dataset — running on a fine-tuned NVIDIA Nemotron model. Investors can use these datasets to identify, analyze and visualize market trends.

## **Speeding Data Pipelines to Improve Fraud Detection**

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs and NVIDIA cuDF help accelerate data processing across multi-terabyte-scale, siloed, regulated sources, compressing the time from data to decision for fraud and other scenarios.

HSBC provides near-real-time client insights that support customer processes and on-demand decision-making while minimizing risk and fraud, powered by 5x faster data processing on [Starburst Enterprise’s GPU Engine](http://starburst.io/press-release/starburst-introduces-torin-gpu-native-analytics-engine-built-on-nvidia-cudf).

Stripe, a global provider of programmable financial services, sees 42x faster data pipelines and 92% cost savings for its Stripe Radar fraud-detection platform with NVIDIA GPU-accelerated Ray Data in offline testing. This enables Stripe Radar’s machine learning pipelines to continuously optimize model training and improve fraud detection.

Title: NVIDIA Cosmos Opens New Tools to Train, Evaluate and Deploy World Models

URL Source: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/cosmos-open-train-evaluate-deploy-world-models/

Markdown Content:
To help developers rapidly build [world models](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/world-models/), which help [physical AI](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/generative-physical-ai/) systems understand and simulate the real world, NVIDIA has expanded the [Cosmos platform](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai/cosmos/) with new training tools, simulation checkpoints and Cosmos Data Factory blueprints.

Ranking top five on six different open models leaderboards, the NVIDIA Cosmos platform gives world model builders the frontier open models — as well as data, training and optimization tools and recipes — to scale training data, adapt models, test behavior and optimize for performance before deployment.

## **Build Better Training Data**

Building world models begins with multimodal, multisensory data.

[NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cosmos-data-factory) brings together the tools and skills for labeling, curating, augmenting and evaluating data at scale for training physical AI. Cosmos Curator, a GPU-accelerated solution for curating video training datasets, has now added support for multimodal multisensory inputs and processing blocks.

Cosmos Data Factory now offers the following five cloud-native blueprints and is available through [GitHub](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cosmos-data-factory), [Microsoft Azure](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-cloud/blog/mobility/automotive/2026/10/21/advancing-autonomous-vehicle-development-with-microsoft-nvidia-porsche-and-voxel51/), [Nebius](https://nebius.com/blog/posts/nebius-expands-physical-ai-workbench-agentic-workflows-nvidia-cosmos%E2%81%A0%EF%BF%BD%E2%80%9D%20with%20%E2%80%9Chttps://nebius.com/blog/posts/physical-ai-workbench) and [CoreWeave](https://coreweave.com/news/coreweave-unveils-coreweave-physical-ai-launchables-taking-the-setup-work-out-of-robotics-and-av-development):

*   **Autonomous Vehicle Dataset Generation:** Curates and labels driving data, then adds synthetic examples of hard-to-capture scenarios to expand training coverage.
*   **Image Attribute Augmentation:** Varies object appearance to improve image search.
*   **Event Video Generation:** Turns still images into synthetic videos of rare or unsafe events.
*   **Defect Image Generation:** Generates printed circuit board, metal and glass defect images for inspection models.
*   **Video Data Augmentation:** Changes weather and lighting in existing footage while preserving scene structure.

Video Player

Companies are already putting Cosmos Data Factory blueprints to work to speed their physical AI development workflows.

Porsche is leading the development of a shared AV data flywheel across Volkswagen Group brands, using Cosmos Data Factory through Voxel51 on Microsoft Azure. This is expected to reduce repeated physical test drives by up to 90% and shorten development cycle times by up to 85%.

_Porsche searching and augmenting autonomous vehicle data footage in Voxel51, powered by Cosmos Data Factory._

ANYbotics generated over 1,500 synthetic video clips with Cosmos Data Factory blueprints, curating real-world data and validating outputs with [Encord’s](https://encord.com/data-labs/nvidia-anybotics-synthetic-data/)platform, to train its industrial-inspection robots to recognize liquid spills and other changes between facility visits.

[Ultralytics](https://www.ultralytics.com/blog/nvidia-cosmos-yolo-synthetic-defect-detection?utm_source=nvidia&utm_medium=referra), a computer vision company, retrained its YOLO model with real images and targeted synthetic defects generated using Cosmos Data Factory, improving defect localization and recall.

## **Train, Adapt and Optimize Models**

With training data prepared, developers may train their own architecture or start with a pretrained model.

At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA extended[Cosmos Framework](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cosmos-framework) training, optimization and deployment tools and recipes as agent skills to more open models, along with Cosmos 3, giving world model builders a faster path from experimentation to deployment.

Developers and agents can now adapt open models like [GR00T](https://developer.nvidia.com/isaac/gr00t), [Alpamayo](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/solutions/autonomous-vehicles/alpamayo/), QWEN, Pi0.5 and other compatible Hugging Face models through fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, optimize the model with distillation and quantization, and deploy with high-performing inference.

Cosmos Framework is an open, modular framework of model training and optimization tools and skills to accelerate world model development.

To develop a world model specialized for egocentric manipulation, robotics research lab MicroAGI post-trained Cosmos 3 on videos of humans manipulating objects and distilled its 32-billion-parameter reasoner down to an 8-billion-parameter Nano model with no loss in accuracy.

Developers can label data and post-train Cosmos 3 on[Roboflow](http://blog.roboflow.com/roboflow-joins-nvidia-cosmos-coalition) for their specific environments and tasks, then deploy those models to RoboFlow hosted or on-premises NVIDIA GPUs to bring video reasoning into factories and warehouses.

Alongside these tools, NVIDIA continues advancing foundational technology through its work on Cosmos models.

New [Cosmos 3 Nano model variants](https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/cosmos3-examples) for simulation enable developers to test autonomous policies in repeatable, hard-to-capture, multiview multisensor scenarios. Accompanying code allows developers to adapt the models to train and evaluate their own policies for autonomous vehicles and bimanual robots in interactive simulations before real-world testing.

ADNOC uses Fogsphere’s MistIQ agentic platform, built with Cosmos and the NVIDIA Metropolis VSS Blueprint, to detect safety hazards in real time across 65 sites. For rare events, [Fogsphere](https://fogsphere.com/fogsphere-scales-ai-agents-at-adnoc/) also uses the Cosmos Data Factory to generate synthetic training data, improving detection without needing to physically stage dangerous situations.

# How Companies Are Using NVIDIA DSX to Break the Power Bottleneck

 Companies around the world are using the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run AI factories as one system and unlock infrastructure development.

October 21, 2026 by[Vladimir Troy](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/author/vtroy/ "Posts by Vladimir Troy")

 Share

Share This Article

Companies around the world are building on the [NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/products/dsx/) to plan, simulate and run the grid and the AI factory as one system, from the substation to the rack. Their adoption of the platform responds to an acute problem.

Power is now the biggest bottleneck in infrastructure. More than $300 billion in equipment is backlogged, and over 200 gigawatts of projects are waiting in U.S. interconnection queues.

One root cause of the bottleneck is siloed systems. The grid, the facility and the compute inside have long been designed independently from one another, creating the conditions for delays, risk and stranded capacity.

To help address this, NVIDIA DSX brings these systems together:

*   **NVIDIA DSX Sim and SimReady assets** from leading energy manufacturers let engineers simulate the grid, substation and AI factory together, validating generators, switchgear, power systems and cooling before breaking ground.
*   [**NVIDIA****DSX Flex**](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/products/dsx/flex/) syncs AI factory demand with grid conditions and onsite generation, turning AI factories from static loads into flexible grid assets.
*   **NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS and DSX Exchange** squeeze more compute from every watt and securely share signals across compute, networking, energy, cooling and operations.

**GE Vernova** is deploying its grid-to-facility and rack power expertise to complement NVIDIA DSX systems, enabling customers to transform power constraints into competitive advantages while maximizing compute and token output, sustainability and grid reliability.

**Hitachi Energy**’s battery energy storage system has qualified as [NVIDIA DSX Ready](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/products/dsx/dsx-ready/), helping customers identify power infrastructure that meets applicable NVIDIA DSX reference architecture design requirements for resilient, reliable and scalable AI factories.

**Schneider Electric**, together with AVEVA and ETAP, is advancing NVIDIA DSX with validated [NVIDIA Vera Rubin](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/technologies/rubin/) power and cooling reference architectures and an [NVIDIA Omniverse](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/omniverse/)-powered AI factory digital twin.

Combining **AVEVA**’s engineering software expertise with NVIDIA SimReady assets, OpenUSD and Omniverse enables connecting simulations, real-time operational data and AI-driven optimization across AVEVA, Schneider Electric and third-party solutions. Together, these capabilities help organizations design, simulate, operate and optimize data centers across their lifecycle, improving energy efficiency and workload performance while accelerating time to token.

**Siemens Energy** is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA by developing a reference design for resilient, scalable and grid-aware power infrastructure across power generation, transmission and distribution. This design is aligned with the requirements of the NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin AI factory design. The company is also exploring usingNVIDIA technologies such as RAPIDS, Metropolis and Isaac Sim for its Noedra digital twin platform, evaluating how the technologies could enhance grid infrastructure monitoring, identify emerging risks and support unplanned outage prevention.

**Phaidra** integrated DSX Flex, DSX Max-Q and DSX Exchange into its self-learning agents, optimizing cooling and power allocation to maximize tokens per watt, improve grid flexibility and deliver about 10% more compute within the same power envelope.

**Emerald AI** integrated its Conductor platform into DSX Flex to help utilities tap underused grid capacity, an approach modeled to unlock up to 100 gigawatts on the existing U.S. grid.

Title: NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations

URL Source: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/european-retail-open-models-robotics/

Published Time: 2026-10-22T05:00:23+00:00

Markdown Content:
European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a digital twin.

## **Frontier Results With Open Models**

Retail leaders and technology companies across Europe are using NVIDIA-accelerated open and frontier models to advance agentic commerce, digital product discovery and retail R&D.

Shopify post-trains open models to reach frontier-level accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Its engineers use the [NVIDIA Megatron Bridge](https://docs.nvidia.com/nemo/megatron-bridge/0.1.0/index.html) library for faster fine-tuning and [NVIDIA NeMo RL](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-data-science/products/nemo/) for reinforcement learning. Shopify has post-trained [NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-data-science/foundation-models/nemotron/) for the GraphQL subagent integrated into Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant for merchants. The subagent retrieves store data for several Sidekick features, including Sidekick Pulse, which researches a merchant’s store and recommends ways to improve it.

On Shopify’s internal benchmark, the post-trained model surpasses a leading frontier model in accuracy while cutting serving costs by 90% and delivering responses 7x faster. Beyond Sidekick, [NVIDIA CCluster](https://docs.centml.ai/home/introduction/) vLLM inference optimization software helped Shopify achieve 4.5x faster performance and up to 12x lower inference cost across five additional use cases: catalog enrichment, merchant assistant, e-commerce shopping simulation, product taxonomy classification, and merchant and buyer recommendations.

Zooplus, Europe’s leading online pet retailer, with Infosys and NVIDIA technologies rebuilt its product discovery stack for the agentic era. A production ready prototype deployed inside Zooplus’ Amazon Web Services (AWS) environment achieved 86% search accuracy using the NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever library for semantic search and the [NVIDIA Blueprint for retail catalog enrichment](https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia/retail-catalog-enrichment) for generated, search-ready product attributes.

Photoroom results from its deployment with Vestiaire Collective, where its Image Editing API now standardizes every primary image, about 40,000 a day across 70 countries, at the point of listing. Listings processed by Photoroom[sold at a 5% higher rate of liquidity, with 3% to 7% more unique views per product page](https://www.photoroom.com/inside-photoroom/vestiaire-collective-liquidity-photoroom). The pipeline runs on NVIDIA GPUs with TensorRT and Triton Inference Server, and NVIDIA Dynamo Snapshot can help users quickly respond to demand spikes.

Omi launched ProductDrop, a workflow that anchors every generated image to an approved digital twin, letting brands [scale creative output across entire catalogs without introducing product errors](https://www.omi.so/resources/blog/omi-productdrop-brings-product-accuracy-to-genai-with-nvidia). L’Oréal is using this approach, combining Omi’s digital twins with generated brand environments within its CreAItech program. Omi runs TRELLIS 3D asset generation on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, speeding up inference by 10x and reducing pipeline latency by 4x.

In addition, L’Oréal is accelerating the discovery of the best ingredient combinations, moving from months of experimentation to hours of computational screening, with the integration of NVIDIA ALCHEMI into its research workflow.

L’Oréal is also testing this approach with CurieOS, Orbital Industries‘ operating system for science and engineering, using OrbMol-v2, its open source molecular simulation model. Integrated with the NVIDIA ALCHEMI Toolkit and powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, OrbMol-v2 is five times faster than comparable models and delivers 21% lower error than the next-best model of its kind. This AI-based workflow enables researchers to identify the most promising ingredient combinations for solubilizing UV filters and optimizing performance before committing to laboratory testing.

Mirakl, a software company for intelligent commerce, runs open models on NVIDIA GPUs, both on its own infrastructure and through European cloud providers like Scaleway. This keeps its [technology sovereign, avoids vendor lock-in and delivers the speed and scale its customers expect](https://www.mirakl.com/blogs/agentic-commerce/why-mirakl-builds-on-open-source-ai-and-what-it-delivers-for-ecommerce-businesses/). Mirakl’s Catalog Transformer pairs fine-tuned open models with proprietary services and has onboarded more than 70 million products, turning messy vendor data into accurate, well-organized catalogs.

## **Physical Intelligence Enables Training in Simulation**

NVIDIA physical AI, digital twins and open models help simulate retail environments, automate warehouse operations and deliver virtual try-on experiences for European retailers and fashion brands.

Otto Group advanced its autonomous warehouse under human supervision initiative — built with Reply on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and running on Google Cloud — to the group’s largest fulfillment center in Haldensleben, Germany. New capabilities let logistics teams [design, test and optimize warehouse operations](https://www.ottogroup.com/en/stories/story/otto-group-advance-the-autonomous-warehouse-with-coala-and-nvidia-omniverse.php) entirely in simulation before any physical implementation.

ALLSIDES launched its 3D Digital Twin Factory: an [automated pipeline](https://www.allsides.tech/resources/allsides-3d-digital-twin-factory) that transforms physical objects into SimReady 3D digital twins in minutes, capturing sub-millimeter geometric accuracy, measured physical properties and fully relightable materials that maintain accuracy under any lighting condition. Those digital twins serve as the foundation for simulating entire store layouts in 3D, as well as for tracking products reliably throughout the shopping journey and at checkout regardless of ambient light. Built on NVIDIA CUDA, OptiX and TensorRT, the platform already serves brands including adidas, Amazon, Nike, Zalando and Zara.

CATCHES achieved production results from its RealFit deployment with AMIRI of [conversion up 55%, add-to-cart up 80% and gross sales up 56%](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261022064337/en/CATCHES-Opens-to-Retailers-with-PredictiveFit-Virtual-Try-On-Launching-on-THE-OUTNET-After-RealFit-Lifted-AMIRI-Online-Conversion-by-55), all after seasonal adjustment against like-for-like styles. The company launched PredictiveFit, extending physics-based virtual try-on to retailers, as well as CASI, a personal fashion agent that shops, styles and sizes for customers over WhatsApp, powered by open weight models including NVIDIA Nemotron 3, built on NVIDIA Omniverse and the Newton Physics Engine.

## **Explore New NVIDIA Retail Blueprints at the****Nebius****Booth**

At GTC Berlin, [Nebius is showcasing three NVIDIA Blueprints for retail](https://nebius.com/blog/posts/retail-ai-agents-nvidia-blueprints-nebius), all available in early access and running on Nebius infrastructure, accelerated by NVIDIA:

*   **Agent Harness for Employee Productivity**: An agentic assistant that consolidates scheduling, task management, inventory alerts and operational insights for store managers.
*   **Inventory Simulation and Optimization:** A blueprint that can help retailers reduce overstock and stockouts by modeling demand scenarios, testing replenishment strategies and optimizing stock levels before users need to commit in the real world.
*   **Agentic Finetuning Flywheel:**A self-improving loop that uses agentic workflows to continuously generate training data, fine-tune open source models and feed real-world performance back into the next training cycle.

# Pioneers Across Europe Deploy NVIDIA Earth-2 Open Models to Power Real-World Weather and Climate Prediction

October 21, 2026 by[Niall Robinson](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/author/nrobinson/ "Posts by Niall Robinson")

 Share

Share This Article

Weather forecasts shape more than daily plans; timely weather information is crucial for energy producers, insurers and transport operators to plan around changing conditions. A global forecast can show a storm taking shape, but decisions about solar farms, shipping routes or insured property depend on what happens locally.

[NVIDIA Earth-2](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/high-performance-computing/earth-2/) gives developers and researchers a family of open AI models and tools they can customize with their own data. Running on NVIDIA computing, these technologies support global weather prediction, detailed regional forecasts and environmental research.

**StormScope EU** is the latest model to join Earth-2 — a regional version of the StormScope model for short-term forecasting, trained over Europe weather and climate data. It uses EUMETSAT satellite observations to predict evolving cloud conditions across 16 Meteosat channels at 10-minute intervals.

At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is showcasing a live StormScope EU pipeline in an interactive weather demo built in partnership with [Earthmover](https://www.earthmover.io/blog/building-a-low-latency-earth-2-nowcasting-pipeline-with-earthmover). The demo uses Earth2Studio to run forecasts and Earthmover’s data platform to manage and serve the real-time results, which are updated as soon as new satellite observations come in, every 10 minutes. Earthmover serves these results as map tiles, letting visitors explore predictions across Europe without downloading entire datasets.

Developers can combine Earth-2 models in workflows tailored to regional needs, using StormScope for short-term forecasting and CorrDiff to add local detail to coarser weather data. Developers can also pick up these model architectures and train them for new environmental applications such as air-quality modeling. The open source [NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo](https://developer.nvidia.com/physicsnemo) framework provides training and customization tools so teams can build applications that incorporate proprietary data and domain expertise to meet regional needs.

Organizations building on Earth-2 capabilities include:

**AXA** is using NVIDIA Earth-2’s FourCastNet 3 to study regional cyclone risk beyond the historical record across more than 1,000 simulated seasons, generating insights that can inform risk assessments and help customers target prevention efforts.

**Vaisala Xweather** is [combining Earth-2 with its proprietary observations](https://www.xweather.com/blog/vaisala-xweather-collaborates-with-nvidia-to-deliver-ai-powered-early-warning-for-high-impact-weather), lightning data and forecasting expertise to enhance its weather intelligence platforms for government, energy, maritime, transportation and insurance customers. Its work includes adapting StormScope with lightning data to advance short-term forecasting lead time and make these warnings accessible through Vaisala Xweather’s software-as-a-service offerings and AI-assistant integrations.

**TotalEnergies** is exploring NVIDIA Earth-2 for solar-energy forecasting, evaluating StormScope-based solar-radiation nowcasts at two photovoltaic sites and developing models to provide weather information at subhourly intervals. The work explores how more detailed forecasts could help anticipate changes in solar-power generation.

**Space42** developed SARDiff4Height using CorrDiff and NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo. The research estimates surface heights from a single radar image and produces uncertainty maps, helping analysts understand where estimates need closer scrutiny.

articles.content:
Title: NVIDIA Open Models Power a New Wave of European Public Sector Projects

URL Source: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/european-public-sector-open-models/

Published Time: 2026-10-22T05:00:02+00:00

Markdown Content:
Governments need modern solutions to serve the public while keeping sensitive information under their control.

Open models provide a path forward, letting governments evaluate them, adapt them to local languages and public services, run them on infrastructure they control, apply their own safeguards and keep sensitive data within controlled environments. Some open models go further, with the datasets they were trained on published so governments can verify if training data was licensed, biased or compliant.

NVIDIA partners and European governments are teaming to bring advanced models to boost the efficiency of public administration while retaining control of data and infrastructure.

Several are also building editions of the [NVIDIA Nemotron-Personas collection](https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/nemotron-personas), the partner-grounded datasets behind [NeMo User Sim](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/UserSim), NVIDIA’s open source library for population-scale user simulation that dynamically evaluates and trains models and agents in local languages.

## **European Commission: Scaling Governed AI Applications**

Berlin-based software company deepset is expanding its [Haystack Enterprise Platform](https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.deepset.ai%2Fhaystack-platform&data=05%7C02%7Cavikanova%40nvidia.com%7Cb1aac5c4554e4102010a08df2b03cf00%7C43083d15727340c1b7db39efd9ccc17a%7C0%7C0%7C639276967559950354%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=2ee0ZpSWJYDNkZL0P1b5YrKYwTB4CKcKtgIATGoZgtc%3D&reserved=0), the foundation of AI@EC, the [European Commission’s shared platform](https://www.deepset.ai/case-studies/european-commission-deepset) for building and running AI applications on commission-managed infrastructure.

The update connects agent development, execution, optimization and governance for all customers, adding capabilities to compare operating costs, evaluate answer quality and trace problems.

[NVIDIA Triton Inference Server](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/triton-inference-server/user-guide/docs/index.html) supports the shared services used to find and rank relevant information. The expansion builds on operating requirements demonstrated by deployments such as AI@EC, where reusable components, role-based access, audit trails and guardrails support applications including document summarization, knowledge management and multilingual policy analysis.

## **Poland: Advanced Computing for Healthcare and Employment**

Deloitte is helping Poland build agentic systems for healthcare and employment services using open models.

Poland’s eHealth Centre is building its Intelligent Services Platform for medical imaging with [NVIDIA DGX BasePOD](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/dgx-basepod/) and the MONAI framework. The tool will help physicians analyze X-rays, CT scans and MRI images, detect abnormalities and prioritize urgent cases, reducing the time patients wait for results.

With Deloitte’s support, Poland’s Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Policy is developing an agentic factory on NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure. Designed to support more than 400 labor offices, it will run models including PLLuM, GPT OSS and Inkling for document search, summarization and digital assistants, helping staff more efficiently assist job seekers.

NVIDIA is also working with SpeakLeash in Poland and the University of Ljubljana in Slovenia on country-specific additions to its synthetic personas program, with localized datasets planned to follow.

## **UK: Data for Locally Relevant Advanced Modeling**

London-based [Locai Labs](https://www.locailabs.com/blog/nvidia-nemotron-personas-uk-technical-report) released [Nemotron-Personas-UK](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-Personas-UK), a dataset of 1 million synthetic personas reflecting the U.K.’s demographic and geographic diversity while reducing privacy risk. Potential uses include healthcare evaluation and bias testing across age groups, education levels and rural and urban populations. For developers building public-service models, it offers a way to test whether models work consistently across different communities.

## **Germany: Digital Assistants and AI for Classified Work**

In Germany, [Materna](http://google.com/url?q=https://www.pressebox.de/pressemitteilung/materna-information-communications-se/materna-stellt-sinfonie-vor-eine-on-premises-plattform-fr-digital-humans/boxid/1317329&sa=D&source=docs&ust=1792606876214470&usg=AOvVaw2rmPdVSxrnuUrumXURJ1jn) is introducing Sinfonie, an on-premises platform combining generative AI, voice interaction and 3D avatars, with [NVIDIA Audio2Face](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-open-sources-audio2face-animation-model/) available for animation. Built on a project for a German state administration, it helps employees access institutional knowledge through spoken questions while keeping data on their organization’s infrastructure.

For organizations handling classified information, secunet, NVIDIA, [Red Hat](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261021042665/en/Red-Hat-AI-Factory-with-NVIDIA-Accelerates-Agentic-AI-Security-Capabilities-Across-the-Open-Hybrid-Cloud) and [deepset](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/deepset-unveils-reference-architecture-for-self-improving-sovereign-ai-agents-on-nvidia-infrastructure-302914982.html) are going a step further. The four companies are developing a sovereign cloud offering built on secunet’s proven SINA Cloud foundation, which includes security components that have been authorized for use with classified information. The planned offering combines four components: NVIDIA accelerated computing and [NVIDIA Nemotron](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-data-science/foundation-models/nemotron/) open models; Red Hat OpenShift AI for deploying and managing AI workloads; deepset’s Haystack AI agent orchestration; and infrastructure operated by secunet in German data centers.

To support local development, [the Sovereign Open Source Foundation Models research initiative](https://www.iis.fraunhofer.de/en/ff/amm/allinga/ai-model-factory/soofi.html) (Soofi) is developing a family of AI models for German industry and the public sector. That includes [Nemotron-Personas-Germany,](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-Personas-Germany) an open dataset of 1 million records, each with six synthetic personas, grounded in the 2022 census across all 16 federal states and 400 districts. Created with [NVIDIA NeMo Data Designer](https://docs.nvidia.com/nemo/datadesigner/getting-started/welcome) without real people’s private data, the dataset helps developers test whether public-service models work consistently across regions, age groups and communities. Like the U.K. edition, it can be used with [NeMo User Sim](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/UserSim/) so developers can evaluate and train models against simulated users based on synthetic German personas.

## **France: Advanced Open Models in the Public Sector Workspace**

CANUT, France’s public purchasing body for digital services, selected [LINAGORA](https://linagora.com/sites/default/files/2026-10/PR_LINAGORA_CANUT_0.pdf) and Docaposte to provide a sovereign collaborative workspace built on Twake.ai.

More than 2,500 eligible organizations, including municipalities, schools and healthcare institutions, can access the framework without running their own tender. The workspace offers public employees email, document sharing and collaboration tools, with NVIDIA technology supporting speech transcription and infrastructure hosted in France. Région Occitanie is the preferred partner for scaling deployment.

## **Greece: A Local Agentic Ecosystem**

Greek AI and energy company [KIEFER](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/from-energy-tokens-european-ai-ecosystem-showcased-nvidia-gtc-ystxe/) is developing an agentic factory built on NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD with DGX GB200 alongside Sophea open weight models and Greek-language tools for knowledge retrieval, speech and digital assistants. These capabilities stand to make institutional information easier to find and use for Greek-speaking public sector teams, while giving organizations control over where agents run and how data is handled.

## **Codefest: Building the Next Applications**

In an effort to support public sector organizations in integrating agentic AI in Europe and beyond, NVIDIA Open Models Codefest brings together startups, software providers and labs across the region to turn open models into locally controlled solutions for public sector challenges, including medical reasoning, AI tutoring and model governance. The top five teams are [Pleias](https://pleias.ai/), [Zehnlab.ai](http://zehnlab.ai/), [Disseqt](https://www.disseqt.ai/), [Algoritmica GmbH](https://algoritmica.ai/) and [ABA Technology](https://aba.technology/en/). [Deutsche Telekom and T-Systems](http://google.com/url?q=https://www.t-systems.com/de/en/insights/newsroom/news/deutsche-telekom-powers-open-models-ai-codefest-across-emea-with-nvidia-1221678&sa=D&source=docs&ust=1792594206181923&usg=AOvVaw0PljEq-38oAirZa6cqYiwu) have provided the compute infrastructure for teams to train and deploy large language models.

articles.title: 1Password launches a way for AI agents to log in on your behalf without seeing your password
articles.summary: The new feature allows agents to log into a customer's personal accounts while still protecting the private credentials that secure those accounts.
articles.content:
Concerns have swirled over the access that consumers are increasingly entrusting to AI agents. Now, security services are trying to catch up.
Password manager 1Password on Thursday launched a new tool by which users can allow agents to log into their personal accounts on their behalf, without the agent ever having access to a user’s credentials.
The new platform, dubbed
1Password for Agents
, accomplishes this by creating a system of communication between the agent, the user, and the password manager. When an agent attempts to log in on a user’s behalf, a unique digital key is sent to 1Password to confirm the agent’s digital identity. The user is then sent an alert about the login attempt and can personally confirm the request. 1Password then signs in the agent, filling in the credentials on the digital assistant’s behalf, which allows it to log in and complete whatever task is at hand.
1Password for Agents allows users to choose their agent of choice — whether that’s Claude Duet from Anthropic, OpenAI’s Dots or ChatGPT Work, Grok Bot, Meta’s Muse, or agents from Town, which is an AI assistant startup. The company says it is working with other companies to expand the service.
“Handing over a password, secret, or credential is a common shortcut to an agent, but can leave people with sensitive information in places they can no longer control as a copy gets saved for the next time,” the company said
in a blog post
. “1Password for Agents gives people a trusted way to delegate tasks to personal AI agents while keeping control of the passwords, secrets, and credentials those tasks require.”
Online agentic activity has increasingly unsettled major institutions. Indeed, 1Password’s new platform is launching on the same day that Axios
reports
that U.S. banks have begun to detect agentic activity inside user accounts.
This isn’t necessarily a case of rogue agents pilfering accounts but, rather, an example of how consumers are increasingly allowing automated services to act on their behalf, including on financial matters. However, the potential for agent-related problems is still large. The big issue appears to be that most banks cannot tell if the agentic activity is tied to user requests or not.
Bankers interviewed by the outlet described the situation as “horrifying,” and a Chase spokesperson interviewed by Axios additionally told the outlet that customers “should not give their usernames and passwords to anyone.”

articles.title: OpenAI makes its Jev competitor widely available as decision model competition heats up
articles.summary: OpenAI is launching its decision model to the world. Can it compete with the original Jev?
articles.content:
OpenAI made its Decisions API model
widely available
to users for the first time, entering the market for fast, cheap intelligence that recently made TypeSafe, a startup founded by a former researcher at the frontier lab, a
$7.6 billion company
.
TypeSafe’s Jev model
created a category
for deep learning models that act as super classifiers: Given a set of options, they can quickly make choices and offer a confidence rating in their decision. Software developers quickly found that these decision or System One models could replace LLMs in a variety of workflows, operating more quickly and a at dramatically lower cost.
Nikunj Handa, the product lead for OpenAI’s APIs, told TechCrunch that his colleagues saw Jev and said “wow, we we have like a million use cases for this.” Handa’s team sprinted to offer their own version: Rather than building a specifically calibrated decision model, the team took ChatGPT Luna and reconfigured it to speed up the inference and lower the cost.
“The big unlock with Decisions API has been the speed, shrinking things from one to three seconds to 100, 120, 180 milliseconds,” Handa said. “In the future, we may sort of like have specific training to make our models like even better in these ways. But right now, it’s just plain old Luna that gets the job done.”
Announced at the company’s developer day on September 29, the Decisions API became available to all customers on Thursday. OpenAI added new voice and visual modalities to the public version, and worked to ensure lower latency in regions around the world by targeting its inference resources geographically.
In initial trials with customers like Box, Datadog, Ramp, and Speak, engineers used the API to replace OpenAI’s LLMs with higher throughput. Andrew Hsu, the CTO at Speak, which builds AI language tutors, said the Decisions API allowed the company to cut the time between actions from 1.4 seconds to .13 seconds. OpenAI also used the product to improve their Dots voice assistant’s responsiveness.
Still, it’s not clear exactly what makes a good decision model, other than “it works for you” — optimization across intelligence, cost, calibration, and speed seems to differ by workload. TypeSafe CEO Diogo Almeida distrusts benchmarks and urges people to trial the models in their own work, but even TypeSafe
released its own rankings
last week alongside the release of its latest Jev model, which includes new features including support for images and smart-if statements.
Public benchmarks like the
AIM System One Index
and the
Artificial Analysis Decision Index
tend to favor D1 Ultra, a new decision model that Liquid released last week, and Base Lab’s Elephant-1. The latest Jev model remains competitive on both indices, in seventh and third, with OpenAI’s Decision Model falling eighth and fourteenth, respectively. However, TypeSafe’s offerings are, for now,
the most widely-queried
on OpenRouter.
The most fun Jev benchmark, however, is
JevMan
, a benchmark where decision models play PacMan; the latest Jev model tops that ranking. Felix Wunderlich, the chief growth officer at Opper AI, which built the benchmark, said the classic game “is an interesting test because of its nonstop stream of quick, high-stakes decisions. At every junction the model must decide where to go in a few hundred milliseconds.”
Where OpenAI’s arguably more capable model may have an advantage is in multi-modality—for image classification, “Luna is extremely powerful and has been showing better calibrations,” Handa told TechCrunch, adding that OpenAI customers want the Decisions API to be more flexible about using images as outputs as well.
Handa also saw further increases in speed enabling new use cases: “Can we get this to something like you know 60 milliseconds, and then you could imagine like an API like call like for every single frame in like a video?”
As these offerings get faster and cheaper, we can expect them to live up to Jev’s namesake, an economist who
explained how
using a resource more efficiently makes it more ubiquitous. Or, as Handa sees it, there will be an expanding “crazy set of use cases” that were hiding in plain sight until the decision models revealed them.

articles.title: Canva releases its first image generation model
articles.summary: Canva is making its new image model available to all users, promising better, more customizable performance at lower costs.
articles.content:
Design platform Canva released its first image generation model, called Canva Craft, developed by its research team to compete with same-category models from Google, OpenAI, ByteDance, and Meta.
The company said its model works in two stages. In the first stage, it interprets users’ prompts and creates a plan with details like spatial relationships of elements, relative scale, visual hierarchy, and information for text generation. In the second stage, its model generates an image of up to 2K resolution in a possible 30 different aspect ratios for various platforms.
Canva said that this approach allows it to create images with accurate details of objects and legible text. Plus, users would be able to make precise edits without changing other parts of the image.
The company noted that rather than using photographs, it used designs to train this model using human-designed templates from Canva’s library, including posters, social posts, presentations, infographics, menus, and typography-rich layouts.
That means images generated with Canva Craft could be converted into layered designs using Canva Magic, the company’s image-to-design transformer. Last year, the platform released its
own model that understands designs and layers
.
Canva Craft is available on the company’s platform to all users, who can access the model from the Dream Lab tab. The model will also be available through the Canva API. Plus, the company plans to support image generation in third-party chatbots like ChatGPT and Gemini through Canva’s MCP.
Canva has used a bunch of image models for generation in its platform, so it’s likely that the new models will help save API costs for the company. It said that besides costs, the new model also allows the platform to have better quality and speed control.
In 2024, Canva acquired
media generation platform Leonardo.ai
. It said that the researchers from Leonardo contributed to the new image model.
Canva said that it is developing two cost-efficient versions of the model, called Craftfast and Craft-ultrafast, which will be released soon.
The company was on track for
$4 billion in revenue last year
. However, it cut its
growth forecast for 2026
, causing its valuation to reportedly
plummet from $42 billion to $35 billion
, according to external analysts.
